request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.

Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the

no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every change that moves a figure is now followed in the audit file by `ROLLUP` and `TOTALS` lines. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works:** the server works out each person's claimed and due-total the same way the screen does, once just before a change and again just after it. It then compares the two:
- **`ROLLUP`:** one line per person whose figures changed, in the order people were added. A newly added person always gets a line. The line uses the person's current name.
- **`TOTALS`:** one line when the sheet's claimed-total or due-total changed.

If nothing moved, nothing extra is written.

**Line format:** the spec labels the name as `person=`, not `name=` as the request words it, so the lines are written as `ROLLUP sheet=<id> by=<user> person=<name> claimed=… due-total=…`. A due-total with no rate shows as `n/a`.

**What changed:**
- **New code** in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/`:
  - `Rollup.java` works out the figures and writes the lines.
  - `TakeRollup.java` takes the "before" snapshot.
  - `AuditRollup.java` takes the "after" snapshot, reading the sheet's today again, and records the lines.
- **Wiring:** all ten endpoints that change data now run a `before` step straight after the sheet is loaded and a `rollup` step after the change's own audit line. These are add/edit person, add/edit claim, open/settle/void, statement, set rate and set today. Changing today gets only the rollup lines, with no line of its own.
- **Refused changes:** an action that's refused stops before the `rollup` step, so it still writes nothing.
- **No changes** to the front end or the database schema.

The person due-total calculation now exists in two places on the server: the new `Rollup` and the existing `TakeStatement`. I left `TakeStatement` alone. If the rule changes later, both need updating unless one is made to use the other.
